articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary: Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

articles.summary: Chess.com is ready to go a lot bigger than chess. After launching Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, earlier this year, the company is now adding 10 more games: backgammon, checkers, go, hearts, mahjong, shogi, sudoku, solitaire, xiangqi, and a Scrabble alternative called word. They're all part of Chess's new Classic Games platform, which is launching […]

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
articles.summary: President Donald Trump promised to put a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said at a […]

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.

articles.title: Local lattice distortion shows promise for designing self-healing alloys
articles.summary: Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) are structural materials with strong mechanical properties, good resistance to radiation damage and broad compositional flexibility. These features make them promising candidates for next-generation nuclear, aerospace and fusion applications. Their development has been hindered, however, by the cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing across a vast range of compositions.

articles.title: Researchers develop smarter way to handle tokens in long-context AI
articles.summary: When we give a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-4, Llama or Mistral, a task such as summarizing a lengthy research paper or a conversation, it first breaks the text into smaller units called tokens. The model then processes these tokens to understand the text and generate a response. Today's LLMs can process inputs exceeding 128,000 tokens. However, processing such long inputs places considerable demands on computing power and memory.

articles.title: 'Self-reflective' robot recognizes its limitations
articles.summary: A new AI model developed by researchers at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) teaches robots to recognize their own limitations. When they encounter an unfamiliar situation they cannot handle, for example, they simply stop and wait for someone to help them. This enables robots to continuously learn new skills without forgetting what they already know or putting people at risk.

articles.title: 'SLIC' training could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
articles.summary: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices.

articles.title: A LEASH for AI-controlled robots: New system could reduce harmful actions
articles.summary: Large language models, the models behind the functioning of ChatGPT, Gemini and similar platforms, are now also used in robotics. These models can help robots to interpret user instructions, plan their actions and respond to changes in their surroundings.

articles.title: Anode-free sodium batteries last longer thanks to an electrolyte that forms its own shield
articles.summary: Sodium batteries, which store and release electrical energy by moving sodium ions between their two electrodes, could be a more affordable alternative to lithium-based batteries. This is because sodium is highly abundant on Earth and can be sourced from widely available raw materials.

articles.title: Movies at 30,000 feet: Hollywood's high-flying market
articles.summary: Airlines carried almost as many passengers last year as cinemas sold tickets worldwide, turning in-flight entertainment into a major market for Hollywood.

articles.title: FBI investigating apparent hack of its key national criminal justice database
articles.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of a national law enforcement database that it maintains, a person familiar with the matter said Saturday.
